_comment: CELPIP Listening Part 2: Listening to a Daily Life Conversation. One conversation, heard once, then 5 questions.

items.title: At the pharmacy
items.context: You will hear a conversation between a pharmacist and a customer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hi there. How can I help you?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hi. I'm here to pick up a prescription for my daughter. The last name is Singh.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Let me check. Yes, I have it here. It's an antibiotic for an ear infection, is that right?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's right. The doctor said she should start it today.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Okay. She needs to take it twice a day, in the morning and in the evening, for ten days. It's important to finish the whole bottle, even if she feels better after a few days.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ten days. Got it. Does she need to take it with food?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes, it can upset her stomach, so give it to her with breakfast and dinner. Also, keep the bottle in the fridge. It's a liquid, and it lasts longer when it's cold.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Okay. And how much is it? Our insurance usually covers most of it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your insurance covers eighty percent, so your part is twelve dollars and fifty cents.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's fine. Oh, one more thing. She has a school trip on Thursday and will be away all day. Is it okay if she takes the morning dose a little later?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's fine, as long as the two doses are at least eight hours apart. If you like, I can give you a small travel bottle so she can take it with her lunch.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That would be great, thanks.

questions.prompt: Why is the man at the pharmacy?
options: To pick up medicine for his daughter
questions.explanation: He is picking up a prescription for his daughter.

questions.prompt: For how long should the daughter take the medicine?
questions.explanation: Twice a day for ten days, and she must finish the whole bottle.

questions.prompt: Where should the medicine be kept?
How much will the man pay?
questions.explanation: Insurance covers 80%, so his part is twelve dollars and fifty cents.

questions.prompt: What does the pharmacist offer to do?
options: Give him a small travel bottle
questions.explanation: She offers a small travel bottle for the school trip.

items.title: Planning a garage sale
items.context: You will hear a conversation between two neighbours.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Morning, Raj! Have you got a minute?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sure, Linda. What's up?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A few of us on the street are planning a group garage sale on the last Saturday of the month. I wondered if you'd like to join.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, that sounds fun. Actually, we've got a lot of things in the basement since our kids moved out. Old toys, a desk, even a bicycle.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Perfect. The more houses that take part, the more people will come. We're going to put an ad online and some signs at the end of the street.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What time would it start?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Eight in the morning until about two. The early morning is when the serious buyers come.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Eight? That's early for a Saturday, but okay. What happens to the things that don't sell?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's a charity truck coming at three to collect anything left over, so you don't have to put it all back in the basement.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's great. My wife will be happy about that. Is there anything I can do to help?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: If you could make a couple of the signs, that would be a big help. I've got the cardboard and markers; I just don't have much time this week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No problem. I'll pick them up from you tomorrow.

questions.explanation: A group garage sale on the last Saturday of the month.

questions.prompt: Why does Raj have things to sell?
options: He is moving to a new house.
questions.explanation: They have many things in the basement since their kids moved out.

questions.prompt: Why will the sale start early?
options: It will be very hot later.
Serious buyers come early in the morning.
The street will close at noon.
questions.explanation: 'The early morning is when the serious buyers come.'

questions.prompt: What will happen to the things that are not sold?
questions.explanation: A charity truck will collect anything left over.

questions.prompt: What will Raj do to help?
questions.explanation: He will make a couple of the signs with Linda's materials.

items.title: Returning a jacket
items.context: You will hear a conversation between a customer and a store employee.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good afternoon. How can I help you?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hi. I bought this winter jacket here two weeks ago, and I'd like to return it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sure. Is there something wrong with it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Well, the zipper broke the second time I wore it. And it's not as warm as I expected. I walk to work, and I was freezing yesterday.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you have your receipt?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes, here it is. I paid with my credit card.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Thanks. Since it's within thirty days, I can give you a full refund to your card. Or, if you like, you could exchange it for a warmer one. We just got a new line of jackets that are rated for minus thirty degrees.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, really? How much are they?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They're two hundred and forty dollars. Your jacket was one ninety, so you'd pay the difference of fifty dollars. But they're on sale until Sunday, fifteen percent off.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hmm. Let me think. Can I try one on?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Of course. The fitting rooms are at the back, next to the shoe section.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with the jacket?
options: The zipper broke, and it is not warm enough.
questions.explanation: The zipper broke and it is not as warm as she expected.

questions.prompt: How does the woman get to work?
Why can she get a full refund?
options: She is returning it within thirty days.
The store is having a sale.
questions.explanation: 'Since it's within thirty days, I can give you a full refund.'

questions.prompt: How much did the original jacket cost?
What will the woman probably do next?
questions.explanation: She asks to try one on, and the employee points her to the fitting rooms.
